evidence.label: HGX B200 server
evidence.note: This is the unit used everywhere in the comparison.

evidence.label: Multi-node fabric
evidence.note: The baseline assumes one 16-server RoCE scheduling domain; the split topology follows the user-defined boundaries.

evidence.label: GLM-5.2 B200 benchmark
evidence.note: NVIDIA reports these operating points for a 64K/400 agentic trace with 90% KV reuse, including P50 user throughput and TTFT.

evidence.label: GLM-5.2 NVFP4 footprint
evidence.note: Useful for feasibility, not a production-concurrency claim.

evidence.label: Deployment packing
evidence.note: Aggregated uses four TP4/DP4 workers. Disaggregated uses three 4-GPU prefill workers and one 8-GPU decode worker. The simulator packs whole units, then fills remaining GPUs with TP4 workers.

evidence.label: RoCE transfer calibration
evidence.note: NVIDIA supports RoCE for production disaggregated KV transfer, but the published GLM-5.2 result used InfiniBand. Measure your fabric and adjust this factor.

evidence.label: DAU conversion
evidence.note: L = λW links average concurrent work, arrival rate, and time in system. Session behavior inputs remain editable.
evidence.source: Little’s Law as Viewed on Its 50th Anniversary

evidence.label: Agent-session behavior
evidence.note: TraceLab’s 4,300-session coding-agent dataset supports using editable prompts and pause time instead of a universal DAU multiplier.

evidence.label: DAU definition
evidence.note: The simulator divides completed sessions by editable sessions-per-DAU to estimate unique users.

evidence.label: Cloud cost anchor
evidence.note: Eight-GPU on-demand price; equivalent to $1,651.20 per server-day before discounts.

evidence.label: Purchase cost anchor
evidence.note: Not NVIDIA MSRP. The owned mode adds the selected facility uplift and amortizes over the selected lifetime.
